+When traversing relations, the ORM will avoid re-fetching objects that were

### Root Cause
When evaluating an outer `prefetch_related` lookup in [`prefetch_one_level`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-rhn0kxco/django/db/models/query.py#L1869-L1966), `prefetcher.get_prefetch_queryset()` is called first before nested `prefetch_related` lookups on the returned queryset are extracted and deferred to subsequent levels. However, in [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-rhn0kxco/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-rhn0kxco/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L365-L382), and [`create_reverse_many_to_one_manager.<locals>.RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-rhn0kxco/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L635-L655), iterating over `queryset` to populate the reverse relation cache caused `queryset` to be evaluated immediately—including its nested `prefetch_related` lookups—and then unconditionally overwrote the reverse relation cache on `rel_obj` with the parent `instance` from the outer queryset.

### Solution
Updated `get_prefetch_queryset()` in [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-rhn0kxco/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L149), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-rhn0kxco/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L379-L382), and [`RelatedManager`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-rhn0kxco/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L650-L653) to check whether the reverse relation is already cached (`is_cached(rel_obj)`) before setting it to `instance`.
